skill.name: flutter-add-integration-test
skill.description: Configures Flutter Driver for app interaction and converts MCP actions into permanent integration tests. Use when adding integration testing to a project, exploring UI components via MCP, or automating user flows with the integration_test package.
skill.summary: Turn Flutter UI exploration into repeatable integration tests with setup, execution, and performance profiling guidance.

content.value_statement: Manual Flutter UI checks are difficult to repeat consistently. This skill guides MCP exploration, integration test authoring, execution, and optional performance profiling.
actual_capabilities: Guide Flutter SDK test dependency setup, Driver extension initialization, and stable widget key assignment.
Guide MCP app launching, widget tree inspection, text entry, tapping, and scrolling.
Translate explored UI flows into WidgetTester integration tests with assertions and frame synchronization.
Provide host driver examples and execution guidance for Chrome, local Android, and Firebase Test Lab.
Explain timeline capture and local performance summary output through a profiling driver.
Address lazily loaded widgets, animation timeouts, and legacy Flutter Driver API differences.
limitations: The skill provides instructions and examples, not a bundled test runner or MCP server.
Interactive exploration requires compatible Dart/Flutter MCP tools and a runnable application.
Device testing requires a configured Flutter environment, available targets, and ChromeDriver for Chrome.
Examples require application-specific imports, widget keys, initialization, and assertions; Firebase uploads remain a separate console step.

use_cases.title: Add Initial UI Regression Coverage
use_cases.description: Configure test dependencies and turn a key application interaction into a repeatable integration test.

use_cases.title: Convert Exploratory Checks Into Tests
use_cases.description: Inspect widgets through MCP, exercise a user flow, and preserve its expected behavior with stable selectors and assertions.

use_cases.title: Investigate Scrolling Performance
use_cases.description: Wrap integration test actions in timeline capture and use the profiling driver to produce local performance summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a First Integration Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Add integration testing to this Flutter project. Inspect existing setup, configure SDK test dependencies, and create a simple test with a host driver.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish basic integration test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Capture an Explored UI Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use available Dart/Flutter MCP tools to explore [user flow] with test data. Add stable widget keys and convert the interactions into integration tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: preserve a manually verified interaction path.

prompt_templates.title: Repair an Unreliable Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [failing integration test] using its failure output. Check animations, lazy widgets, and selectors. Apply focused fixes and rerun on [target device].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: diagnose synchronization and visibility failures.

prompt_templates.title: Profile a Scrolling Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Add timeline capture around [scrolling journey] with binding.traceAction(). Adapt the profiling driver to summarize scrolling_timeline data and report local output paths.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: collect performance evidence from an integration test.

output_examples.input: Add an integration test for the sample counter screen.
output: Test dependencies and a host driver are prepared for the application.
The test checks an initial counter value of zero, taps the increment button, waits for frames, and expects one.
Execution status is reported separately, including any missing device or environment requirements.

output_examples.input: A test cannot find an item near the bottom of a lazy list.
output: The diagnosis identifies that the item is not mounted until the list scrolls.
The test scrolls the correct container until the keyed item is visible, then interacts and checks the resulting state.
The result summary distinguishes code changes from verified test execution.

output_examples.input: Prepare performance profiling for a scrolling test.
output: The test journey is paired with timeline capture and a matching profiling driver.
The driver summarizes the captured timeline and writes local timeline output with a performance summary.
Measured performance results require running the instrumented test.

best_practices: Use a dedicated test entry point for Driver instrumentation and keep production entry points free of test-only initialization.
Assign stable widget keys and synchronize frames or scrolling before interactions and assertions.
Run tests with nonproduction data on the intended target, and review failures before claiming successful coverage.
anti_patterns: Assuming MCP tools, ChromeDriver, or device targets are available without checking the environment.
Applying pumpAndSettle blindly when infinite animations prevent the application from settling.
Copying sample imports, widget names, or timeline keys without adapting them to the actual application.

faq.question: Which testing package does this skill use?
faq.answer: It focuses on integration_test with flutter_test and WidgetTester. It also explains API differences for legacy flutter_driver tests.

faq.question: Does the skill include an MCP server?
faq.answer: No. Interactive exploration requires compatible Dart/Flutter MCP tools configured separately.

faq.question: Can it guide Chrome and Android test execution?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents ChromeDriver setup, Flutter drive commands, and Android APK preparation for Firebase Test Lab.

faq.question: Does it automatically upload tests to Firebase?
faq.answer: No. The documented Firebase workflow instructs users to upload the application APK and test APK through the Firebase Test Lab console.

faq.question: Why can a visible list item be missing from a test?
faq.answer: Lazy lists may not mount off-screen widgets. The guidance uses scrolling to mount the target before interaction.

faq.question: Are passing tests or profiling results guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on the application, configured environment, selected device, and actual test execution.
